findings.evidence: Original: recharts' default accessibilityLayer made the chart <svg> a tabIndex=0 role=application element inside the role=img wrapper. Now: `<BarChart data={rows} accessibilityLayer={false} margin=...>` and `<LineChart data={buildRows(data, series)} accessibilityLayer={false} margin=...>`.
findings.why_it_matters: Verified against recharts 3.8.1 sources, not just the tests: CartesianChart.js:24 default `accessibilityLayer: true`; :43 `resolveDefaultProps(props.categoricalChartProps, defaultCartesianChartProps)` only replaces `undefined` (resolveDefaultProps.js:45 `acc[key] === undefined && dp[key] !== undefined`), so an explicit false survives; :73 reports it to the store (rootPropsSlice.js:27); accessibilityContext.js:4 `useAppSelector(state => state.rootProps.accessibilityLayer) ?? true` returns false (?? does not coerce false); RootSurface.js:47,52 then yields `tabIndex = hasAccessibilityLayer ? 0 : undefined` and `role = hasAccessibilityLayer ? 'application' : undefined` = undefined/undefined, and the chart's otherAttributes do not contain tabIndex/role. keyboardEventsMiddleware.js:36,148,174 also disables the arrow-key handling when the prop is false. A tree-wide grep of recharts/es6 shows the only remaining tabIndex values are -1 (Pie sectors, TooltipBoundingBox, ZIndexPortal) and Brush (0, role=slider), and Brush is not used; so the svg is no longer a tab stop and nothing focusable remains inside role=img. Tests: TrendChartsRecharts.test.tsx:107-108 and :189-190 assert `accessibilityLayer === false` and no tabIndex prop on both charts (stub-level; the real effect is established from the source above, real DOM remains a Phase 9 check). JSDoc on both components explains why (tooltip is pointer-only, keyboard users read the sr-only table).
findings.required_action: Resolved. Keep 'chart svg is not a tab stop, no role=application' in the Phase 9 browser checklist.

findings.evidence: buildRows: `const touchesPartial = datum.partial === true || data[index + 1]?.partial === true || data[index - 1]?.partial === true;` and `row[partialKey(item.key)] = touchesPartial ? value : undefined;` (solid key still `datum.partial ? undefined : value`). createPartialDotRenderer(color) returns a renderer that draws `<circle cx cy r={DOT_RADIUS} fill="var(--surface-card)" stroke={color} strokeWidth={LINE_STROKE_WIDTH}/>` only when `isPartialRow(payload)` and cx/cy are numbers; the dashed Line uses `dot={createPartialDotRenderer(toneColor(item))}`.
findings.why_it_matters: Re-traced by hand. Lone partial [P]: dashed key has the value, the renderer draws its marker (visible). Middle partial [A,B*,C]: rows (solid,dashed) = (1,1),(-,2),(3,3): solid A and C with a gap at B, dashed A-B-C, so both segments touching B are dashed and A, C keep the solid line's markers. Trailing [A,B,C*]: (1,-),(2,2),(-,3) unchanged from before. Consecutive partials [B*,C*] join to the complete points on both outer sides only. Complete points that only neighbour a complete point are not dashed. Joining complete points get no extra marker because the renderer filters on payload.partial (no double dots), and a partial point has no solid dot (solid value undefined), so there is no overlap. Typing is sound: payload narrowed with `typeof === "object" && !== null && "partial" in payload && payload.partial === true`, no any, no assertion. cx/cy null (gap) fall to null. A new renderer closure per series per render is negligible (a handful of series, charts re-render on data change only). buildRows is now exported for direct testing; 8 new tests in TrendLineChartRows.test.tsx (6 buildRows cases covering lone, middle, neighbour-only, trailing, no-partial, partial:false; 2 renderer cases including exact SVG and null guards) match the code I traced and are not vacuous. File is 156 lines, component 64 lines.
